findings.evidence: Use when generating frontend or SDK types from openapi.yaml/openapi.json (including FastAPI, springdoc or NestJS output)
findings.fix: Convert OpenAPI 3.0.x JSON/YAML specs into TypeScript types for components/schemas and for each operation's parameters, request body and responses, plus runtime type guards on request; Swagger 2.0 and OpenAPI 3.1 input (including FastAPI 0.99+ default output) is detected and refused with the reason. Use when generating frontend or SDK types from openapi.yaml/openapi.json (springdoc, NestJS or other 3.0 generators), typing the endpoints under paths, updating types/api.ts after the spec changed, or deciding how nullable, readOnly/writeOnly, oneOf/discriminator, allOf, additionalProperties or $ref map to TS, even when the user only says 'API types' or 'typed responses'. Keywords: OpenAPI 3.0, components/schemas, types/api.ts, type guard. Not for standalone JSON Schema or Zod conversion, non-TypeScript targets, HTTP clients, mock servers, or validating a spec without emitting types.

List only eval inputs from evals/files/ in `files`, for both spec-types and shapes-guards. references/guards.md is part of the skill, not an input, so listing it here hides whether the skill's own loading trigger works.

findings.evidence: If it is listed, run `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`.
findings.fix: After the project check, also run `npx tsc --noEmit --strict --target es2022 <out>`, or add `--strict` when the project tsconfig has `strict` or `strictNullChecks` off. A non-strict project config hides `| null` and optional-property errors, so the validation loop can pass types that fail for strict consumers. The worked example also claims it passes `tsc --strict`.
